title: Walking through a wood: the chest rule, per row vs per rect
question: He is holding right the whole time in both. Which reads like a gnome walking through a wood — and does the one that goes further ever look like he is cheating through solid ground?
context_md: DISCRETE COUNTS. Cells travelled over the 600 ticks after he sets off: A=98, B=357 (acceptance bar 200). On main today he stops permanently at x=107 from frame 6,600 to 18,000 — the blocker is ONE soil cell at (108,194), rejected at every step-up lift because lifting slides the offender DOWN his body and it needed one row more than step_up reaches. Sweep over 6 start frames (min/median cells): 0 -> 1/44, 2 -> 44/93, 3 -> 49/94, 4 -> 50/161, 5 -> 51/166, 6 -> 47/47 (6 is a cliff: he sinks into the floor). 849 tests pass, clippy clean. STILL OPEN, not fixed here: at the worst window he stops against a soil bank 5 cells abreast at chest height with nothing hard in it — the wade model has no way over a powder face.
